items.title: Dick Katz interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: So I used to sit in with a trumpet player named Stanford East, and he had this little quintet

ctx.x: Okay. Well you found yourself pursuing music, I wonder if your parents were in favor of that?

Oh well my father was a very creative duck. He was very eccentric and I was well prepared for all the crazy people I was going to be involved with. My whole family is a little bit crazy, except my sister, she was a straight arrow. And my brother went to a place — you probably never heard of — Black Mountain College, but that was a place in North Carolina, it was almost like a commune. And they had really prestigious people teaching there but it was very small. Anyhow no, they weren’t. My mother was sure I would…
